claim: src/_pytest/pathlib.py puts a samefile_nofollow implementation detail in the docstring instead of a code comment.

findings.claim: src/_pytest/pathlib.py puts a samefile_nofollow implementation detail in the docstring instead of a code comment.

evidence_receipt.claim: src/_pytest/pathlib.py puts a samefile_nofollow implementation detail in the docstring instead of a code comment.
evidence_receipt.expected_stdout_contains: # On Windows st_ino is the file ID, which file systems are free to not support,
evidence_receipt.falsification_condition: The st_ino implementation detail appears as a code comment (lines 58-62), while the docstring (lines 53-56) only describes the function's contract, contradicting the claim. The claim would be supported only if the st_ino detail appeared inside the docstring.

verification_result.stdout:
# On Windows st_ino is the file ID, which file systems are free to not support,
    # in which case it is 0 for every file -- WinFsp mounts such as sshfs-win are one
    # example. os.path.samestat() would then consider any two files on the volume to
    # be the same (python/cpython#78116), so treat a zero file ID as "unknown" and
    # leave the caller with plain path comparison (#14864).
